title: Autoscaler Policy Orchestrator: metric bindings, algorithm modes, and hard-safety caps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement the Autoscaler Policy Orchestrator (APO) to support pluggable target metrics, selectable scaling algorithms, and enforceable safety limits for Dedicated fleets. This ticket covers design, API surface, simulator, and an initial implementation that supports route+model scoping, percent-based fallbacks, and operator-configured hard caps. Problem: current autoscaler is a single-mode heuristic that causes oscillation on bursty workloads and provides no single source of truth for safety limits across Dedicated pools. We need a modular engine that lets SRE/Customers choose target metrics (latent p99, tokens/sec, queued requests, GPU util) and algorithm modes (target-based PID, gradient-step, predictive with short horizon), and then enforce guardrails (min/max nodes, scale rate limit, cooldown windows, burst reserve).
acceptance_criteria: APO can bind a scaling policy to a route+model combo via the API
Support for at least three target-metrics: p99 latency, tokens_per_second, and queued_requests
Implement two algorithm modes: target-PID and predictive short-horizon (10s forecast), selectable per-policy
Safety limits applied cluster-wide and per-policy: min_nodes, max_nodes, max_scale_per_minute, cooldown_seconds
Simulator reproduces workload traces and produces stable decisions for existing test traces (no oscillation >3x in 10m window)
End-to-end canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated pools with observability dashboards and automatic rollback on SLA regressions
design_notes: Key design choices: 1) Modeled metrics: prefer closed-loop signals (p99, queued) plus open-loop (tokens/sec) for capacity planning. 2) Algorithms: PID tuned per-policy using historical trace calibration; predictive model is simple EWMA+trend to avoid ML drift. 3) Safety: enforce hard caps at decision stage and in actuator to avoid race conditions. 4) Scoping: policies can be applied at route, model-variant, and pool level with inheritance and explicit overrides. 5) Observability: emit decision_reason, computed_target, and confidence to tracing for post-mortems.
tradeoffs:
- Full ML-based prediction would be more accurate on 5-30m horizons but introduces complexity and risk; we choose lightweight predictive heuristics for now.
- Enforcing very tight cooldowns reduces responsiveness on sudden sustained load; we provide burst_reserve to handle short spikes.
- Per-policy tuning increases configuration surface; default recommended policies will cover 80% of customers.
implementation_steps: Design APO API and proposal doc (this ticket)
Build simulator harness and port historical Dedicated traces
Implement algorithm modules: pid_controller and predictive_ewma
Add safety limit enforcement in decision-layer and actuator-level checks
Wire up policy stores and UI config surface in Console (config-only for canary)
Create dashboards and alerts for decision stability and SLA regressions
Canary rollout and follow-up tuning; collect feedback and iterate
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for controller math and safety enforcement. 2) Simulator regression tests against legacy traces (include at least three customer workloads: bursty chat, steady-throughput embedder, mixed RLHF-style). 3) Integration tests: policy binding -> decision -> actuator with mocked infra. 4) Chaos tests: delayed telemetry and duplicate decisions to ensure idempotent actuator behavior. 5) Canary: deploy to 10% of Dedicated capacity for 72h with automated rollback on 5%+ SLA regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal teams only (SRE + Platform customers) for 2 weeks. Phase 2: opt-in beta customers on Dedicated for 4 weeks. Phase 3: global default for new Dedicated pools with opt-out for existing pools after 2-week notice. Emergency rollback via console toggle to revert to legacy autoscaler per-pool.
